advances: A finite weighted centerpoint with a strict original minimal-face mass alternative for midpoint-closed labels.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Work in the finite-dimensional affine hull of $P$. Intersecting ambient closed halfspaces with this hull gives intrinsic halfspace traces, allowing the whole trace, and every intrinsic halfspace extends by extending its affine functional. Thus the resulting depth is independent of this restriction. If $P$ is a singleton, then $k=1$ and its depth and face weight both equal $M$, as claimed. For the rest assume $P$ has at least two points.

Use the general finite-set lemma in the proof of accepted fact $\texttt{bee3cc8e50a0dcea}$. It bounds the Helly number for traces of arbitrary convex sets on $P$ by the maximum size of a subset $R\subseteq P$ with every member a vertex of $\operatorname{conv}R$ and $P\cap\operatorname{conv}R=R$. Two distinct points of $R$ of the same label have a midpoint in $P\cap\operatorname{conv}R$ that is not a vertex, contradicting these properties. Thus $|R|\le k$ and the Helly number is at most $k$. Apply the generic finite-support construction in accepted fact $\texttt{c6b7777f667984de}$ in the affine hull of $P$, with closed location set $T=P$, Helly bound $h=k$ and probability $\sum_{p\in P}(w_p/M)\delta_p$. Its finite support is $P$, and it gives a point of $P$ with depth at least $M/k$ after rescaling. This construction applies to every positive weight vector on the same $P$.

Put $\alpha=M/k$. For each $p$, the depth $\delta_w(p)$ is the minimum over the finitely many traces on $P$ of closed halfspaces containing $p$. For any weight vector $w'$ this gives $|\delta_w(p)-\delta_{w'}(p)|\le\sum_{q\in P}|w_q-w'_q|$. If $F_p$ is proper, a supporting halfspace exposes it with trace exactly $P\cap F_p$. If $F_p=Q$, its weight is the total. In both cases $\delta_w(p)\le w(F_p)$, and the same inequality holds for $w'$.

Outside the stated exception, the balanced-face alternative gives a vector $v$ of total zero with $v\cdot\chi_F<0$ for every face $F$ of original weight $\alpha$. If there is no such face, the condition is vacuous and we may use $v=0$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the weights $w'=w+\varepsilon v$ are positive with total $M$. The finite-trace estimate keeps every point whose old depth is below $\alpha$ below $\alpha$ for $w'$. Each face whose old mass is below $\alpha$ stays below $\alpha$ for small enough $\varepsilon$, since there are finitely many faces. Every face of original mass exactly $\alpha$ is strictly below $\alpha$ for $w'$ by the strict inequalities for $v$. Choose one $\varepsilon$ satisfying all these conditions. Take any point of depth at least $\alpha$ for $w'$. Its old depth is at least $\alpha$, and its minimal-face weight for $w'$ is at least $\alpha$. Therefore its old minimal-face weight is strictly greater than $\alpha$.

In the exception each atom has weight $\alpha$ and every closed halfspace containing it captures at least that atom. Its singleton vertex face gives the upper bound $\delta_w(p)\le\alpha$. For $|P|=k$ the nonexceptional cases also have direct witnesses. If any atom exceeds $\alpha$, its own depth and face weight are at least that atom. Otherwise every weight equals $\alpha$, and a nonvertex point has depth at least its atom and has another point of $P$ in its minimal face.

If $\Lambda=c+L$ and $P=Q\cap\Lambda$, two points of the same coset modulo $2L$ have midpoint in $\Lambda$ and $Q$, hence in $P$. The group $L/2L$ has size $2^{\operatorname{rank}L}$. Affine lattice isomorphisms preserve occupied cosets, halfspace traces and faces. In the lifted graph, the displayed midpoint identities put the actual geometric midpoint of the two graph points in the graph. They are required for every distinct same-parity pair. The label of the midpoint can differ from that of the two endpoints.
statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a real affine space with $k$ occupied labels. For every pair of distinct points of the same label, assume their geometric midpoint belongs to $P$. Give the points positive weights $w_p$, with total $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ whose relative interior contains $p$, allowing $Q$ itself. Write $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ and let $\delta_w(p)$ be the minimum weight in any closed affine halfspace containing $p$. The whole-space trace is allowed and is the sole trace containing $p$ in rank zero.

There exists $p\in P$ with $\delta_w(p)\ge M/k$. Such a point can be chosen with $w(F_p)>M/k$ except exactly when $P$ consists of $k$ vertices of $Q$ of weight $M/k$ each. In the exception every point has $\delta_w(p)=w(F_p)=M/k$. In particular, strict minimal-face mass holds for some center whenever $|P|>k$.

For a finite nonempty complete subset $P=Q\cap(c+L)$ of an affine lattice, the labels can be the occupied cosets modulo $2L$. Then $k\le 2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$, including rank zero. For a finite graph $P=\{(p,g_p):p\in P_0\}$ over an affine-lattice base, the labels can be the occupied base parities if every distinct same-parity pair $p,q\in P_0$ has $m=(p+q)/2\in P_0$ and $g_m=(g_p+g_q)/2$. In this graph case the depth and the minimal face are taken in the lifted space.
title: A weighted midpoint-label center with strict minimal-face mass
